newsitem.title: UK: DHL says UK-US volumes up on UPS strike.
newsitem.headline: DHL says UK-US volumes up on UPS strike.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said it is receiving increased calls from customers regarding express shipments from the United Kingdom to the U.S. as a strike by United Parcel Service Teamsters continues for a second day.

"We are starting to see the increase in UK-U.S. volumes we predicted, somewhat earlier than expected. This can only gain momentum as the week continues if customers find that there is indeed disruption to UPS service schedules," Glyn Jones, DHL UK Commercial Director said a statement.

"Whilst industrial action is currently limited to the U.S., should there be an overspill to Europe via the Teamsters, we believe our network is flexible and robust enough to meet customers' needs," he added.
The statement said that in the United States, DHL has seen an increase in volume of more than 25 percent, as shippers search for alternatives.

The company has made several adjustments to its U.S. network to cope with additional volume, including the acquisition of temporary aircraft, increasing aircraft flights and hiring more temporary employees.
DHL Worldwide Express comprises DHL Airways, Inc., which serves the U.S. and its territories, and and DHL Iinternational Ltd, which directly and indirectly covers the rest of the world.
